deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. Nothing on it can be restated as a computation. It is a short, heavily corrected prose draft on method.

(a) Heading area (top four lines). These are cramped, abbreviated notes, apparently an outline. I cannot decipher them with certainty. The middle line seems to end in '...-' and the next in '...-[?]'. They look like topic or chapter headings, not formulas.

(b) Heading 'Methode', followed by a struck-through first attempt: 'Die [?] Methode des [?] muss sich ...'.

(c) Main paragraph, reconstructed sense; uncertain words are marked:
- When one works through ('Aufsuchen / Durchgehen') a mathematical proof, the struck-through phrase being replaced by 'Kette von Schlüssen', two quite different activities of the mind must be distinguished.
- In the first, only the understanding (Verstand) is active. One checks each single inference and convinces oneself of its correctness. But one does not see the motives of the individual steps; one follows the prescribed path blindly.
- At the end, the result is only the conviction of the truth of what was proved.
- In the second, one surveys the whole and rises gradually from the individual links of the chain to an overview of the structure ('Gefüge'?) of the whole.
- While in the first activity the mind behaves receptively and critically (checking), the second activity is reproductive and productive.
- The paragraph breaks off with 'Bei ...'.

(d) The lower third of the page is written upside down, in a cramped, partly abbreviated hand. It is a separate draft and is essentially illegible to me. It does not visibly contain formulas.

Context: the next page, 16r/17r, is Riemann's well-known critique of Fechner's Zend-Avesta. That critique also contrasts two methods: induction plus testing of general laws, versus analogy and Anschaulichkeit. This page is evidently an earlier methodological draft for that discussion. It contrasts step-by-step verification with synoptic, productive comprehension. The preceding page, on German historiography, seems unrelated.

results.what: Distinction between two mental activities in following a proof: (1) step-by-step verification of each inference by the understanding, yielding mere conviction of truth; (2) a synoptic grasp of the motives and of the structure of the whole chain, called reproductive and productive.
results.modern_name: Verification vs. understanding/insight in mathematical proof (philosophy of mathematical practice; cf. the logic vs. intuition distinction)
results.usually_credited_to: A commonplace of 19th-20th c. methodology; famously elaborated by Poincaré (Science et méthode, 1908), Hadamard (1945), Pólya (1945). Earlier versions appear in Descartes (Regulae, enumeratio) and Leibniz.

results.what: Methodological contrast that frames the Fechner critique on the next page: induction/abstraction of general laws versus analogy and vividness of the overall picture.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann; fragments on Fechner and on psychology/metaphysics are printed in Gesammelte Werke (Weber-Dedekind, 1876/1892)
